added.nōrma: Traupman’s form (p. 165, checked in the local text of the book), named in the “against” of the norma note as records.md requires; the card says only “Traupman’s long ō is not followed”. It is not used as a term or example.

A cross-reference on the bucket card to the stairs / ladder card (entry-88), which carries the word itself; kept as a related link on bucket.

flags: Overlaps with cards in other batches, recorded here anyway: ladle (culina entry-257 also gives trulla = ladle, Traupman 71; the concept belongs in culina, kept in officina as the card's category); bucket, spade and shovel (ludi entry-180: situla, sitella, pāla); tool (culina entry-128: īnstrūmentum); shears (vestitus entry-320 gives forfex for scissors and points to the shears card); pipe (culina entry-257: fistula, water pipe, Traupman 124); hook (domus entry-87 has uncus vestiārius for a clothes hook, kept here only in a comment; ludi entry-530 points to the hook card for hāmus); the hook-onto example also stands on aedificatio entry-173. Culina entry-119 gives rudicula for a kitchen spatula, so spatula here has the sense “spreading blade”.

Suspected errors in the cards, copied as they are: cochleam evolvere lacks the long ē (Lewis & Short ēvolvō; entry-146 itself writes ēvolve); perforaculum lacks the long ā (Lewis & Short perfŏrācŭlum, from perforāre). furfuraculum is not in Lewis & Short; if it is the same -āculum formation it needs the macron too.

Periods chosen where the card is not explicit: cōchlea / cochlea modern for the threaded fastener (the card: later technical Latin), although Vitruvius has the press screw; trulla (trowel) post-classical on Palladius; perforaculum late (Lewis & Short: post-classical, Arnobius); furfuraculum and īnstrūmentum cochleīs extorquendīs modern as the later period. The card takes the latter “from Latham”, which in Morgan–Owens is the medieval word-list (its sources run to the 17th century), so it may be medieval or Renaissance. capsa clāvōrum and bacillum aduncum are classical: free phrases of classical words that the card does not call ours.
Tape measure leads with taenia mēnsūrālis, which the card's example uses and for which it gives the only explicit attestation (Morgan–Owens, citing Levine); the card lists fūniculus metricus first.

norma: the note records the card's departure from Traupman's nōrma (p. 165; his p. 168 prints norma). The only grounds given are Lewis & Short's unmarked vowel and the readers' spelling; the Greek behind the word (γνώμων, or Lewis & Short's γνώριμος) has ω, which may be why Traupman marks it long. No ruling covers it.

Vitr. 7.2.2: Lewis & Short files this ascia under “a mason’s trowel” (with Pall. 1.14); the card reads it as the adze, which quemadmodum māteria dolātur supports. Worth a look before the quotation is used in a reader.

spatula: the local Adumbratio (the older Morgan–Owens) gives rudicula (Col. 12.46.3) s.v. spatula; the card's claim that Morgan–Owens records spatula rests on the newer site, which could not be opened from here.

Wind up / unwind: the card gives no lemma, only the imperatives involve and ēvolve in its examples, so no verb records were made; both examples are on reel, with the Lewis & Short links for involvo and evolvo.

The card cites Dā mihi, ōrō, ūtendum malleum, tata! as “after Pont. Progymn. I 35; quoted in Libellus VII”. The example's source is the formal Libellus VII citation, which check_libelli.py requires; the Pontanus origin is a line in the hammer record's sources.

Grammar is given by hand where the builder cannot read it from the form: malleus (the builder reads malleī as fifth declension, because it ends in -eī: a bug for every second-declension noun in -eus), the slash forms cōchlea / cochlea and terēbra / terebra, forceps (m./f.), rūgae f. pl., mētior (mēnsus sum) and aduncus. The slash forms, kept as the cards print them, get no word page; the cooking-pot pattern “x (y), gen.” would give them one.
Left out of the skimming-blade comment: “The flat, wide red-handled tool in the earlier photograph is this type”, which refers to a photograph shown in conversation, not on the card.

Senses chosen to keep headwords apart from likely records elsewhere: nail (fastener), file (tool), level (instrument), plane and square (carpenter’s tool), nut (for a bolt), pipe (plumbing), spatula (spreading blade), cord (small rope), strike (hit).
